subject: Usage-sensitivity modeling & next actions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@payflux.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Usage-sensitivity modeling & next actions

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and we can move to a concrete pilot scope. High-level notes: 

Pain points you called out:
- Token cost volatility on peak days (spikes of ~3x baseline on promo nights) causing surprise overages.
- Strict latency requirement for fraud-check flow (p95 target <250ms) but many other flows are batchable or async.
- Concern about unanticipated token growth as new features roll out.

Goals you stated:
- Keep p95 for fraud-checks under ~250ms with <5% error/fallback rate.
- Reduce monthly inference spend from current vendor by ~30–50% while preserving quality.
- Start with a scoped pilot in Q3 to validate economics and latency for the user-facing path.

Initial cost/TCO sketch (very coarse — see attached spreadsheet for scenarios):
- PayFlux reported ~300M tokens/mo baseline (approx). Using their current endpoint configuration we estimated ~USD 18k/mo.
- With recommended levers (continuous batching for non-latency flows, prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, and a midline quantized variant for low-risk calls) we model a 40–50% reduction in token spend in typical scenarios -> ~USD 9–11k/mo.
- If PayFlux opts for a small Dedicated pool for the latency-critical fraud-check path, that adds a fixed capacity cost but reduces per-token and reduces tail latency variability; our scenario 3 in the spreadsheet shows net savings and tighter p95 control for heavy promo nights.

Recommended levers (prioritized):
1) Split traffic by SLA: dedicated low-latency pool for fraud-checks + hosted/pooled path for bulk features.
2) Apply prefix/KV caching on 60–70% of requests with stable prefixes (we saw that ~65% of your sample are templated prompts).
3) Aggressive batching on async workflows (we modeled 2–5x effective per-token cost reduction depending on queueing policy).
4) Offer a quantized model tier for non-critical flows (minor quality delta in low-risk calls).

Immediate asks / next steps we recommended on the call:
- PayFlux: share a 7–14 day sample of traffic (histogram by endpoint, sequence-length distribution). You already said you could export this — thanks.
- Redwood: we’ll run two scenarios (hosted-only + hybrid dedicated) and return a one-page economics summary and a pilot SOW. Lauren will own the financial model; Sean will prepare a sandbox and synthetic replay.
- Schedule: propose a 45–60 minute follow-up the week of Aug 31 to validate numbers and walk the SOW.

Attached: redwood-cost-sensitivity-payflux.xlsx (cost scenarios), redwood-proposed-sow-payflux.pdf (draft SOW).

If any item above is off, please flag. Otherwise we’ll proceed with the data request and return the modeled scenarios by EOD Aug 28.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172
From: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@payflux.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@payflux.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage-sensitivity modeling & next actions

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Budget: we’ve got a constrained Q4 inference budget (roughly $50k for the year left to allocate across experiments). Any pilot needs to fit into that envelope or come with a clear exec-level ROI case.
- Latency: the fraud-check flow is critical — if p95 goes above ~250ms even for short windows during promos we get pager escalations. That path must be isolated.
- Data share: I’ve attached a 7-day sample export (payflux_token_sample.json). It’s redacted but includes endpoint, token count, and timestamp buckets.

We’d like you to focus scenario modeling on two outcomes: (A) hosted + caching/batching only, and (B) hybrid with a small Dedicated pool for fraud-check. Please emphasize worst-case promo night behavior (we can provide the promo schedule if helpful).

Also, procurement asked about contract flexibility — can Redwood do a 3‑month pilot with an easy opt-out and limited committed spend? They want to avoid long lock-ins.

Thanks, Maya
Maya Thompson | Head of Product Integrations, PayFlux
maya.thompson@payflux.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@payflux.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage-sensitivity modeling & next actions

Thanks Maya — got the sample, appreciate the prompt turnaround. Quick confirmations & owner assignments: 

- Procurement ask: yes, we can structure a 3‑month pilot with an opt-out clause and a capped committed spend. I’ll include contract language in the SOW draft for an easy exit and a short notice period.
- Modeling: Lauren — can you run two scenarios (hosted-only + hybrid dedicated) with a worst-case promo night stress test and surface p95 estimates for fraud-check? Please include sensitivity to token-growth + 3-month ROI.
- Sandbox: Sean — please replay the attached token sample in a sandbox and capture p95 distributions for the dedicated-vs-pooled paths.

Maya — propose a 45-minute walkthrough on Tue Sep 1 at 11:00am PT to review the scenarios and the SOW. Does that work for your team? If not, suggest two alternative time slots.

Action owners and timeline summary:
- PayFlux: provide promo schedule (if available) — Maya (by Aug 25)
- Redwood (finance + SE): deliver scenarios + draft SOW (by Aug 28) — Lauren / Sean
- Follow-up meeting: Tue Sep 1 11:00am PT (tentative)

If that aligns I’ll ship the SOW and the modeled spreadsheet by EOD Aug 28. Looking forward to it.

Best — Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172
